walkthroughs.body_html:
The high-energy end of the spectrum is dangerous.

Ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are ionising — they carry enough energy to knock electrons off atoms in your cells. That can damage DNA and cause cancer.

Radio, microwaves, infrared and visible light are non-ionising. They can still harm you (microwaves heat tissue, IR can burn skin) but they don't ionise atoms.

UV: from the Sun and sunbeds — causes sunburn, premature ageing, and skin cancer. Sunscreen helps. ☀️

X-rays: used in medical imaging, but radiographers stand behind lead screens because too much exposure damages cells.

Gamma: highest energy. Used to kill cancer cells in radiotherapy and to sterilise medical kit, but very dangerous in large doses.

Exam questions love asking which EM wave for a given job. Tips:

Communication over long distance with no line of sight → radio. Through-atmosphere comms to satellites → microwaves. Cooking food and detecting heat → infrared. Seeing bones → X-rays. Sterilising equipment → gamma.

Always justify with a property — "radio diffracts around hills", "gamma kills bacteria because it's ionising".

mcqs.q: If one EM wave has a higher frequency than another, what is true about its wavelength?
options: Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
It is shorter — wavelength and frequency are inversely related (c = f x lambda).
It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
It is also longer, because both increase together.

mcqs.q: Which has the longer wavelength: microwaves or radio waves?
options: It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
They have the same wavelength because both are used for communication.
Radio waves — they sit at the longest-wavelength end of the EM spectrum.
Microwaves, because they are used in 'big' devices like radar.

mcqs.q: Why are infrared cameras used to detect warm objects in the dark?
options: It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
Infrared cameras shine infrared light onto objects so they reflect back visibly.
Warm objects emit infrared radiation due to their temperature; the camera detects this emission.
